title: Cover the Board With Dominoes

concept.title: Always cover the first empty square, in one of two ways
body: A *domino* covers two squares that share an edge: two side by side (horizontal) or two on top of each other (vertical). Count the ways to cover **all free squares** of a board with dominoes, with no overlap. Different orders in which the same dominoes are placed must not be counted twice. The trick: always cover the **first empty square** in reading order. Whatever domino covers it, it must be one of two: the square to its right, or the square below it. (The square on the left or above is already covered.)

body.code:
def tilings(pos):
    while pos < r * c and covered[pos // c][pos % c]:
        pos += 1                          # find the first empty square
    if pos == r * c:
        return 1                          # nothing is left: one tiling
    row, col = divmod(pos, c)
    total = 0
    covered[row][col] = True
    if col + 1 < c and not covered[row][col + 1]:       # horizontal
        covered[row][col + 1] = True
        total += tilings(pos + 1)
        covered[row][col + 1] = False
    if row + 1 < r and not covered[row + 1][col]:       # vertical
        covered[row + 1][col] = True
        total += tilings(pos + 1)
        covered[row + 1][col] = False
    covered[row][col] = False
    return total

body: Choosing the *position first, then the piece* is a general way to count tilings without duplicates: every tiling is built in exactly one order. A hole (`#`) is just a square that is covered from the start. An odd number of free squares gives 0 at once. A 6 by 6 board has 6728 tilings.

statement: A board has `r` rows and `c` columns; some squares are holes (`#`) and the others are free (`.`). Count the ways to cover every free square with dominoes (each domino covers two free squares that share an edge, dominoes do not overlap, holes stay uncovered). Two tilings are different if some domino position differs.
inputFormat: Each of the next `r` lines has `c` characters, `.` or `#`.
outputFormat: Print the number of tilings (it can be 0).

examples.note: Two horizontal dominoes or two vertical dominoes: 2 tilings.

hints: Find the first free square (in reading order) that is not covered yet.
Try a horizontal domino to the right and a vertical domino below.
Mark the squares of the domino before the recursive call and unmark them afterwards.

explanation: The function finds the first uncovered free square and covers it with a horizontal domino (if the right neighbour is free) or a vertical domino (if the square below is free), recursing after each. Every tiling is built in exactly one order, so none is counted twice.
solution.complexity: Time proportional to the number of partial tilings (small for 6 by 6), space O(r * c).

code.python:
def tilings(covered, r, c, pos):
    while pos < r * c and covered[pos // c][pos % c]:
        pos += 1
    if pos == r * c:
        return 1
    row, col = divmod(pos, c)
    total = 0
    covered[row][col] = True
    if col + 1 < c and not covered[row][col + 1]:
        covered[row][col + 1] = True
        total += tilings(covered, r, c, pos + 1)
        covered[row][col + 1] = False
    if row + 1 < r and not covered[row + 1][col]:
        covered[row + 1][col] = True
        total += tilings(covered, r, c, pos + 1)
        covered[row + 1][col] = False
    covered[row][col] = False
    return total

r, c = map(int, input().split())
board = [input().strip() for _ in range(r)]

covered = [[ch == "#" for ch in row] for row in board]
print(tilings(covered, r, c, 0))
